BDS degree does not mean wife is earning, Gujarat High Court awards ₹50,000 monthly maintenance to wife and daughter

The Gujarat High Court has awarded ₹30,000 per month to a wife and ₹20,000 per month to her four-year-old daughter, rejecting the argument that the wife should be denied maintenance merely because she holds a BDS degree.

The Court found that there was no material showing that the wife was presently earning sufficient income. Her professional qualification by itself could not establish financial independence, particularly when the husband’s own matrimonial pleadings described her occupation as household work.

The High Court also held that the wife’s separate maintenance proceeding under Section 144 BNSS did not bar her from seeking interim maintenance under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act. Maintenance remedies under different statutes may coexist, subject to adjustment or set-off where an amount has already been awarded elsewhere.

The Court was particularly critical of the husband’s financial disclosure. It found that he had left crucial portions of his income affidavit blank despite material showing business income, shops, insurance policies and other financial resources. Referring to his attempt to portray the wealth as belonging primarily to his family, the Court described him as a “poor son of a wealthy father.”

Finding prima facie concerns regarding incomplete financial disclosure, the High Court directed the Registry to place the matter before the appropriate Bench dealing with contempt proceedings. Apart from monthly maintenance, it awarded litigation and travel expenses and imposed ₹50,000 in costs on the husband.
comment: A qualification cannot automatically be equated with earning capacity. Courts also have to examine access to work, career interruptions, childcare responsibilities and the actual financial position of both parties.
